STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of mixed salad greens (arugula-like leaves with thin shredded carrot) in a white square bowl, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The bowl is a square-ish bowl about 22 cm across its width. Vessel area ≈ 22 x 22 ≈ 480 cm² (using the square footprint; the bowl's interior is slightly smaller, so I use ~400 cm² of usable surface).

STEP 3 - Items: (1) mixed leafy greens (arugula/mixed salad leaves), (2) shredded carrot strips. No visible dressing or oil sheen.

STEP 4 - Area: Greens cover about 15% of the bowl's usable area (~60 cm²). Carrot shreds are scattered within the greens, about 1% (~4 cm²). Total food coverage ≈ 16%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Greens 60 cm² x 4 cm pile height ≈ 240 ml gross volume. Carrot is embedded within the pile, so it is counted in the same envelope: 4 cm² x 3 cm ≈ 12 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Leafy greens 240 ml x 0.15 g/ml ≈ 36 g. Carrot 12 ml x 0.6 g/ml ≈ 7 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Leafy greens ≈ 25 kcal/100 g → 36 g ≈ 9 kcal. Carrot ≈ 41 kcal/100 g → 7 g ≈ 3 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The visible pile is a modest handful of leaves, so a total of about 43 g and about 12 kcal is plausible. It is a light side salad, not a full meal.
